context.title: The Jerusalem Council
context.summary: Some insist Gentile believers must be circumcised. Apostles and elders meet in Jerusalem; Peter, Barnabas, Paul and James speak, and the council sends a letter freeing Gentiles from circumcision. Paul and Barnabas then part ways.
context.background: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17), so requiring it of Gentiles meant asking them to become Jews. The four requests in the letter (vv. 20, 29) resemble laws in Leviticus 17–18 for foreigners living among Israel, which may have helped Jewish and Gentile believers share meals.

customs.note: Meat from animals not properly drained of blood was forbidden to Israel since Noah's day (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:10-14).

watchFor: Peter: 'through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they' (v. 11).
James quotes Amos 9 about rebuilding David's tabernacle (vv. 16–17).
'It seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us' (v. 28).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Barnabas
people.summary: Son of consolation, the surname of Joses, a Levite (Acts 4:36). His name stands first on the list of prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (13:1).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Silas
people.summary: Wood, a prominent member of the church at Jerusalem; also called Silvanus. He and Judas, surnamed Barsabas, were chosen by the church there to accompany Paul and Barnabas on their return to Antioch from the council of the apostles and elders (Acts 15:22), as bearers of the decree adopted by the council.

people.name: Judas
people.summary: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council (Acts 15:22, 27, 32).

people.name: John
people.summary: The evangelist; “John whose surname was Mark” (Acts 12:12, 25). Mark (Marcus, Col. 4:10, etc.) was his Roman name, which gradually came to supersede his Jewish name John.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Phenicia
places.summary: (Acts 21:2) = Phenice (11:19; 15:3; R.V., Phoenicia), Gr. phoinix, “a palm”, the land of palm-trees; a strip of land of an average breadth of about 20 miles along the shores of the Mediterranean, from the river Eleutherus in the north to the promotory of Carmel in the south, about 120 miles in length.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Antioch (Syria)
places.summary: In Syria, on the river Orontes, about 16 miles from the Mediterranean, and some 300 miles north of Jerusalem. It was the metropolis of Syria, and afterwards became the capital of the Roman province in Asia.

places.name: Cilicia
places.summary: A maritime province in the south-east of Asia Minor. Tarsus, the birth-place of Paul, was one of its chief towns, and the seat of a celebrated school of philosophy.

places.name: Syria
places.summary: (Heb. Aram), the name in the Old Testament given to the whole country which lay to the north-east of Phoenicia, extending to beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris.

places.name: Pamphylia
places.summary: Paul and his company, loosing from Paphos, sailed north-west and came to Perga, the capital of Pamphylia (Acts 13:13, 14), a province about the middle of the southern sea-board of Asia Minor.

places.name: Cyprus
places.summary: One of the largest islands of the Mediterranean, about 148 miles long and 40 broad. It is distant about 60 miles from the Syrian coast. It was the “Chittim” of the Old Testament (Num. 24:24).

events.title: Jerusalem Council
events.summary: Passage: Acts 15:1–34. People: Silas, Judas, James, Simon, Barnabas, Paul. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Second Missionary Journey
events.summary: Passage: Acts 15:1–18:23. People: Simon, Paul, Luke, Silas, Barnabas, Timotheus and others. Lasted about 3 years.

events.title: Paul and Barnabas part ways
events.summary: Passage: Acts 15:35–39. People: John, Barnabas, Paul. Place: Cyprus, Antioch (Syria).

events.title: Second Missionary Journey begins
events.summary: Passage: Acts 15:40–41. People: Silas, Paul. Place: Syria, Cilicia, Antioch (Syria). Lasted about 1 month.
